Elias Thorne had lived on the jagged promontory of Blackwood Point for thirty years, a solitary sentinel against the roaring Atlantic. His world was defined by the rhythmic sweep of the great lens, the smell of brine and kerosene, and the relentless howl of the wind. He spoke to no one, save for the gulls and the occasional supply boat captain who dropped off crates of canned goods and mail.
